description_full: Autodesk, Inc. engages in the provision of 3D design, engineering, and entertainment technology solutions worldwide. The company offers AutoCAD Civil 3D, a surveying, design, analysis, and documentation solution; Autodesk Build, a toolset for managing, sharing, and accessing project documents for streamlined workflows between the office, trailer, and jobsite; Revit, a software built for building information modeling to help professionals design, build, and maintain energy-efficient buildings; Autodesk BIM Collaborate Pro, cloud-based design collaboration and design management software; BuildingConnected, a SaaS preconstruction solution; and Tandem, a cloud-based platform that transforms the built asset lifecycle. It also provides AutoCAD software, a customizable and extensible CAD application for professional design, drafting, detailing, and visualization; AutoCAD LT, a drafting and detailing software; Fusion, a 3D CAD, computer-aided manufacturing, and computer-aided engineering tool; Inventor, a software solution that offers a set of tools for 3D mechanical design, simulation, analysis, tooling, visualization, and documentation; product design and manufacturing collection tools; and Vault, a data management software for managing data in one central location, accelerate design processes, and streamline internal/external collaboration. The company offers Flow Production Tracking, a cloud-based production management software; Maya software that offers 3D modeling, animation, effects, rendering, and compositing solutions for film and video artists, game developers, and design visualization professionals; Media and Entertainment Collection that offers end-to-end creative tools for entertainment creation; and 3ds Max software, which provides 3D modeling, animation, and rendering solutions. It sells its products and services through a network of resellers and distributors. Autodesk, Inc. was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

financial_summary: Autodesk, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $55.3B market cap on $7.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 44% against a 11% cost of capital — a 33-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 90% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $2.4B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.18× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 20× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 11% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 22% operating margin runs 15pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.94x).
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 22% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 17% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 1.30, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.53 vs 5y 1.39), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $444.0M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 35% in the 2020 crash, 42% in the 2022 bear market and 76% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $212 (margin of safety -24%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $149 to $309 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 34.3 vs 27.4 and EV/EBITDA 23.5 vs 17.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 46% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 34 covering analysts target $308 on average, 17% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 44% clears the cost of capital of 10.6% by 33pp, the mark of a value creator.
It runs a 90% gross margin and converts 33% of revenue into free cash flow, or 22% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.18x.
ROE of 37% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (4.1x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 22.8% of revenue on R&D and 10.9% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $97.0M (0% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 0.85 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 12.9% over 3 years, 13.7% over 5 years and 11.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 59% of profits supports about 25.9% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 12.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.18 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 14%.
Capex runs only 0.2x depreciation (0.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only bought over the past year (5 purchases, net $2.2M bought).
It returns 2.3% a year to shareholders (2.3% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 0.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 14,300 employees, each generates about $504K of revenue, 1.4x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 8.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $168K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.8M (6x revenue per employee).
